html:
The Johor Sultanate was founded in 1528 by a son of the last sultan of Malacca, after the Portuguese took his father's city (see Portugal takes Malacca).

For a century Johor fought the Portuguese and the rising sultanate of Aceh, moving its capital along the Johor River and to the Riau islands. It allied with the Dutch to take Malacca in 1641; see the siege of Malacca.

Johor ruled much of the southern peninsula and the islands until the 18th century, when Bugis nobles came to dominate it. The Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 split its lands; the mainland became modern Johor.
